function.description: This function extracts all key-value pairs in a JSON object that follow a specified key until it encounters a new nested object or array. It is intended for use within a specific data analysis context that keeps track of the current position within the JSON structure. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

ctx.description: The data analysis context object which contains the current position and functions to navigate through the JSON structure. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

message.content:
Sure! To pull out all the key‑value pairs that come right after the `userId` key in your `dataAnalysisContext`, you can use the `getNextKeyValues` helper.  
Here’s how you’d call it:

```json
{
  "ctx": "<YOUR_JSON_STRING>",
  "currentKey": "userId"
}
```

Replace `<YOUR_JSON_STRING>` with the actual JSON string of your `dataAnalysisContext`.  
For example, if your context looks like this:

```json
{
  "userId": 12345,
  "name": "Alice",
  "email": "alice@example.com",
  "profile": {
    "age": 30,
    "city": "Wonderland"
  },
  "preferences": ["news", "updates"]
}
```

You would call:

```json
{
  "ctx": "{\"userId\":12345,\"name\":\"Alice\",\"email\":\"alice@example.com\",\"profile\":{\"age\":30,\"city\":\"Wonderland\"},\"preferences\":[\"news\",\"updates\"]}",
  "currentKey": "userId"
}
```

Once you pass that to `getNextKeyValues`, it will return all the key‑value pairs that follow `userId` until it hits a nested object or array (in this case, it would return `{"name":"Alice","email":"alice@example.com"}`).
